cases.name: accepted
cases.note: A valid file. doctor prints no block at all.

cases.name: discarded-marketplace-source
cases.note: The incident key: extraKnownMarketplaces.<id>.source written flat.

cases.name: field-dropped-hooks
cases.note: Fails the schema, and enabledPlugins still applies.

cases.name: discarded-permissions-deny
cases.note: The second whole-file case, and the one carrying a Suggested fix line.

cases.name: dropped-over-discarded
cases.note: Two files, two validities, one doctor run. settings.json is field-dropped and says true; settings.local.json is discarded and says false. Honouring the local file, or voiding settings.json, each give false.

cases.name: discarded-many-entries
cases.note: The incident key again, in a file that decides six things: two plugins, one skill, and three .mcp.json server entries. Recorded so the cost figure a finding prints can be wrong in more than one way.

cases.name: deny-nonstring-elements
cases.note: The second partial-acceptance message, and the one that carries no note: "Non-string value in deny array was removed". doctor reports it, and the file still applies. "Bash" is in the array so this also pins that a real rule survives the removal (DEA-150).

cases.name: allow-nonstring-elements
cases.note: The same template on a second key, so the recogniser is reading a message shape and not the word "deny". Also partial acceptance, also no trailing note.

cases.name: dropped-field-and-elements
cases.note: Both partial-acceptance shapes in one file, because they cost different things: `hooks` goes whole, and three elements come out of `permissions.deny` while "Bash" stays. One doctor entry covers all three removals, so the number can only come from the file. The file decides two entries elsewhere (one plugin, one skill), and neither cost figure is 2, so a detector charging the whole file cannot agree with one charging the dropped key.

cases.name: mixed-known-and-unknown
cases.note: One recognised partial acceptance and one nobody recognises, in the same file: `hooks: 42` says "This field was ignored." and 2.1.224's marketplace message says something neither family covers. `validityOf` is a lattice, so the file is `not-checked` -- and it still carries a `field` error, which is the only shape in which a detector guarding on the error alone would report a file whose fate was never established.

cases.name: hook-entry-ignored
cases.note: A third partial-acceptance message, found on 2.1.224: `hooks.PreToolUse` says "This entry was ignored." and the file still applies. No pattern recognises it, so it classifies `not-checked` carrying schema errors -- the failure direction DEA-151 chose, which until this recording had no first-party instance and could only be constructed.

cases.name: valid-local-over-discarded
cases.note: The mirror. settings.json is discarded and says false, the local file is valid and says true. Both parse, so this one passes without any validity check -- it is the control, not the catch.
